headline: TSMC is reported to be planning a further 3% to 6% price rise on advanced chip wafers for early 2027 because demand for its newest process is outrunning supply.
score_reason: Single report relaying DigiTimes with no TSMC confirmation; kept at the pool level.
importance_line: Higher wafer prices feed into the cost of AI and phone chips and push designers such as Qualcomm and AMD to consider Samsung, but this is an unconfirmed report and Samsung's yields are still a target.
summary: DigiTimes, the Taiwanese trade outlet, reports, as relayed by Technetbooks, that TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, is preparing a further price rise of 3% to 6% on advanced wafers, the silicon discs chips are cut from, for the first quarter of 2027, after earlier rises of 10% to 20%. Orders for its 2 nanometer process are said to have exceeded expectations, leading customers such as Qualcomm and AMD to consider Samsung as a second source; the report does not say TSMC has confirmed any of this.
notes: Credit chain: Technetbooks rests on DigiTimes; not independently confirmed.
